rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken verb for frightening or intimidating someone, without stressing the degree or method.

example.english: Someone suddenly shouted behind me and it could terrify me.
example.traditional: 佢突然喺我後面大嗌，嚇親我。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dat6 jin4 hai2 ngo5 hau6 min6 daai6 aai3 haak3 can1 ngo5

rows.note: Use this colloquial expression when someone is frightened extremely badly, literally ‘scared to death’.

example.english: That lightning just now really did terrify me.
example.traditional: 啱啱嗰下閃電真係嚇死我喇。
example.jyutping: ngaam1 ngaam1 go2 haa6 sim2 din6 zan1 hai6 haak3 sei2 ngo5 laa3

rows.note: Use this when the frightening is deliberate intimidation or a threat, especially in more serious contexts.

example.english: That man used the phone to terrify the shop owner.
example.traditional: 嗰個人用電話恐嚇店主。
example.jyutping: go2 go3 jan4 jung6 din6 waa2 hung2 haak3 dim3 zyu2

rows.note: Use this for the menace or threat itself, rather than the immediate feeling of fear it causes.

example.english: His threat to retaliate was meant to terrify me.
example.traditional: 佢話要報復，呢個係對我嘅威脅。
example.jyutping: keoi5 waa6 jiu3 bou3 fuk6 ni1 go3 hai6 deoi3 ngo5 ge3 wai1 hip3
